usageNotes: Creates a scheduled realm-sync job that periodically imports users and/or groups from an external authentication domain (e.g., LDAP, AD) into Proxmox. The `schedule` field uses systemd calendar event syntax (e.g., `daily`, `0/6:00`) and is required. The caller must hold `Realm.AllocateUser` on the target realm and `User.Modify` on `/access/groups/`; this is a cluster-level config write and returns null on success (not a UPID — the job runs on its own schedule, not immediately).

examples.summary: Create a nightly LDAP sync job that enables new users and removes vanished entries

params.comment: Nightly sync of all users and groups from company LDAP

tips: The `id` must conform to pve-configid format (alphanumeric plus hyphen/underscore, max 64 chars) and must be unique across all realm-sync jobs.
Set `remove-vanished` cautiously: including `properties` will strip custom PVE attributes on existing users that are not present in the LDAP source.
This endpoint creates the job definition only — to trigger an immediate sync run, use the separate run/trigger endpoint for realm-sync jobs.
The `realm` body param must match an existing authentication domain configured under Datacenter > Permissions > Realms.
Disabling `enable-new` (set to false) lets you review imported accounts before they can log in, useful for staged rollouts.
